section_summary: This section chiefly contains constituent protests, congressional referrals, and State Department replies concerning continued U.S. petroleum exports to Japan while the United States aided China and prepared for possible war. The Department repeatedly explains that aviation fuel, lubricants, and most gasoline were subject to export licensing and that licenses were denied when shipments threatened national defense; several replies also dispute a Waco Record claim that fourteen million barrels were shipped daily. The section also includes U.S.–Japan telegrams about proposed congressional restrictions, cross-references concerning strategic materials, and further inquiries about oil transport and war-material exports.

subfiles.title: Jack J. Lande to Michigan congressional representatives concerning exports to Japan
subfiles.to: Arthur Vandenberg; Prentiss M. Brown; William W. Blackney
subfiles.about: Lande protests the contradiction between aiding China and supplying petroleum and other materials to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Jack Lande asks Michigan representatives why the U.S. reportedly ships over a million barrels of oil monthly to Japan while aiding China.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to Senator Brown of the Lande correspondence
subfiles.about: Hull acknowledges Brown's transmission of Lande's letter and promises prompt consideration.
subfiles.summary: State acknowledges Senator Brown's correspondence on shipments to Japan and aid to China, promising prompt attention.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Senator Brown on petroleum export controls
subfiles.about: Hull explains the licensing controls governing petroleum exports and returns Lande's letter.
subfiles.summary: Hull says high-octane aviation fuel and aviation lubricating oil were prohibited for most destinations beginning in July 1940, and that licensing was later extended to nearly all gasoline. He adds that applications are assessed for national-defense consequences and that controls and licensing policy are continually adjusted.

subfiles.title: Senate referral of constituent correspondence to the State Department
subfiles.about: The Senate refers an enclosed constituent communication for consideration and a report.
subfiles.summary: The printed referral asks the Department to give the enclosed communication favorable consideration. It requests that a report accompany the returned enclosure, and the following page records filing information.

subfiles.title: W. W. Chapman to Senator Connally protesting petroleum exports
subfiles.about: Chapman asks why the United States continues supplying petroleum to Japan while drafting Americans and aiding countries resisting Japan and Germany.
subfiles.summary: W. W. Chapman cites Commerce figures of 817,733 barrels of petroleum products exported to Japan in March 1941 and calls it intolerable to prepare young Americans for war while supplying potential enemies.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Senator Connally concerning Chapman's letter
subfiles.about: Hull describes petroleum export licensing and the national-defense review applied to shipments to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Hull explains that aviation gasoline and lubricants were restricted in July 1940 and that licensing subsequently expanded to nearly all gasoline. He says no license is issued when a proposed shipment is judged detrimental to national defense and returns Chapman's letter.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Senator Connally concerning T. W. Helm
subfiles.about: Hull explains export controls and rejects the Waco Record's account of gasoline shipments to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The letter repeats the Department's explanation that petroleum exports are licensed and reviewed for national-defense effects. It states that Commerce Department foreign-trade statistics demonstrate the inaccuracy of the Waco Record's claims and returns Helm's letter and the editorial.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to Senator Connally concerning W. W. Chapman
subfiles.about: Hull acknowledges Connally's communication about Chapman's objection to petroleum exports to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Hull acknowledges Connally's May 22 communication and Chapman's letter, promising prompt attention.

subfiles.title: Senate referral of the Helm correspondence
subfiles.about: The Senate forwards an enclosed communication for consideration and a report.
subfiles.summary: Senate referral of the Helm correspondence asks favorable consideration and a report when the enclosure is returned.

subfiles.title: T. W. Helm to Senator Connally about a Waco Record editorial
subfiles.about: Helm asks Connally to stop alleged daily shipments of fourteen million barrels of gasoline to Japan.
subfiles.summary: T. W. Helm encloses a Waco Record editorial claiming fourteen million barrels of gasoline go daily from the West Coast to Japan and asks Connally to protect the U.S.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to Senator Connally concerning T. W. Helm
subfiles.about: Hull acknowledges Connally's communication concerning Helm's claims about gasoline shipments.
subfiles.summary: Hull acknowledges Connally's May 22 communication on Helm's letter, promising prompt attention.

subfiles.title: D. F. Cleary inquiry about China and Japan
subfiles.to: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.about: Cleary requests information about measures affecting supplies to Japan in view of American financial assistance to China.
subfiles.summary: Degraded note from D. F. Cleary contrasting assistance to China with dealings with Japan and asking what steps are being taken.

subfiles.title: Senate referral of the Royston correspondence
subfiles.about: The Senate refers Royston's enclosed communication for consideration and a report.
subfiles.summary: The form asks the State Department to consider the attached material and report on it. The second page carries the file number and filing stamp.

subfiles.title: H. V. Royston to Senator Connally protesting gasoline exports
subfiles.about: Royston urges Connally to halt alleged large-scale gasoline shipments to Japan.
subfiles.summary: H. V. Royston cites a Waco Record report of fourteen million barrels of gasoline shipped daily to Japan, calls it un-American, and asks Connally to oppose it.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to Senator Connally concerning H. V. Royston
subfiles.about: Hull acknowledges receipt of Royston's complaint about gasoline shipments to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Department confirms receipt of Connally's May 21 communication and Royston's letter. Hull promises prompt attention to the request.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Senator Connally concerning H. V. Royston
subfiles.about: Hull explains petroleum export controls and disputes the Waco Record's shipment figures.
subfiles.summary: Hull outlines the licensing of aviation fuel, lubricants, and nearly all gasoline and states that applications are rejected when detrimental to national defense. He adds that official Commerce Department statistics expose the inaccuracy of the Waco Record statement and returns Royston's letter.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to Senator Connally concerning R. S. Claypool
subfiles.about: Hull acknowledges a letter from R. S. Claypool concerning oil shipments to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Department records receipt of Connally's May 26 communication transmitting Claypool's letter. Hull says the request will receive prompt attention.

subfiles.title: Cordell Hull to Jesse H. Jones on petroleum exports
subfiles.about: Hull responds privately to Jones's concerns about petroleum-product exports to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Hull apologizes to Jesse Jones for the delayed reply to his May 7 letter and says petroleum exports to Japan remain under consideration.

subfiles.title: Tokyo Embassy telegram reporting Japanese press reaction to U.S. oil bills
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The embassy reports Japanese press coverage of congressional proposals to restrict petroleum shipments to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Tokyo telegram: newspapers report three measures would stop oil cargoes for Japan and require Commerce permits; the Yomiuri warns a crisis in relations if they become law.

subfiles.title: State Department telegram to Tokyo explaining congressional petroleum measures
subfiles.about: The Department details House and Senate proposals addressing petroleum exports and Axis acquisition of strategic materials.
subfiles.summary: The telegram summarizes Congressman Weiss's bills and resolutions to prevent petroleum shipments to Japan or place them under Commerce Department licensing. It also reports Senator Gillette's proposal for a joint congressional investigation into Axis acquisition of essential war materials from the Western Hemisphere.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on strategic materials shipped from the Philippines
subfiles.about: The sheet points to a memorandum about possible shipment of strategic materials through Asian destinations to Germany.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: strategic materials sent from the Philippines to Japan, China and Asiatic Russia might be reshipped to Germany.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Thomas W. Lamont letter on war materials for Japan
subfiles.about: The sheet points to correspondence criticizing the supply of American war materials to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Thomas Lamont's letter enclosing James Young's criticism of war materials supplied to Japan.

subfiles.title: Senator Maloney to Secretary Hull forwarding the Winchester inquiry
subfiles.about: Maloney asks the State Department to help him answer Winchester's questions about an article on oil shipments to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Senator Maloney sends Hull Benjamin Winchester's letter, a San Francisco Chronicle article on U.S. oil ferried to Japan and his preliminary reply, asking information for a fuller answer.

subfiles.title: Benjamin S. Winchester to Senator Maloney on oil shipments and tanker shortages
subfiles.about: Winchester asks whether an enclosed account of oil shipments to Japan is accurate and how such shipments can be justified amid a domestic tanker shortage.
subfiles.summary: Winchester, for a small discussion group, asks a factual explanation of continued oil supplies to Japan, noting tanker shortages force costly rail movement of Texas oil.

subfiles.title: Senator Maloney's preliminary reply to Benjamin S. Winchester
subfiles.about: Maloney says he will seek the State Department's assessment before answering Winchester's inquiry.
subfiles.summary: Maloney tells Winchester he has submitted the Chronicle oil-to-Japan question to Hull and will report the response.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to Senator Maloney concerning Benjamin S. Winchester
subfiles.about: Hull acknowledges Maloney's request for information about Winchester's concerns over oil shipments to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Hull acknowledges Maloney's May 22 letter and Winchester's inquiry, promising prompt attention.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to Senator McFarland concerning L. E. Holladay
subfiles.about: Hull acknowledges a Tucson constituent's inquiry about oil shipments to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Hull acknowledges Senator McFarland's May 16 letter on L. E. Holladay's correspondence, promising prompt attention.

subfiles.title: Greenville inquiry to the Secretary of the Navy about Japanese purchases
subfiles.about: The writer asks whether Japan is purchasing war materials from the United States and whether American merchant shipping is involved.
subfiles.summary: Handwritten Greenville letter to the Navy Secretary asks confirmation of Japanese purchases of American war materials and whether American merchant ships are used.
